note: COUNTS ONLY. Where the decision engine's positives-only repository groups come from, before any change. Memory = the static example rows of the RustFS store as of the 2026-10-02 slice-2 rebuild (904 examples); labels = the 2026-10-02 regeneration (6,589 rows, identical in counts to 2026-10-01-decision-engine-labels-advisory-fixes); feature records = the 924 static records of the store; harvest units = the merged units of the corpus and advisory harvests. Every (family, group) of the memory that holds positive and no negative example was traced back: negative label row present? feature record for it? excerpt of it? The reason is the first link that is missing. A second table accounts for the pair sides that have a label but no example at all (those groups are absent from the memory on BOTH sides, so they do not show as positives-only; they are where the fixed-side negatives the matcher owes come from). No candidate, path, function, commit or repository name is recorded here; the per-group detail stays in scratch.

reasons.ruby under the record's language: build_features stores the closed feature-vocabulary language (schema.LANGUAGES; `other` for Ruby, Go, C#); the memory build hands that `other` to the excerpt matcher, which then runs the brace matcher: a Ruby `def` has no brace body, so 7 pairs (14 sides) get no excerpt; 4 further Ruby pairs (8 stored examples) matched a `{ |x| ... }` block inside the method instead of the method -- 2-line excerpts, wrong spans. The 11 Go pairs (22 examples) under `other` are brace-matched to the exact body (a correct span) and 9 C# pairs likewise.
